Start, stop and inspect the daemon.

The daemon serves the project commands on /home/you/.wdx/wdx.sock. It reads the settings when it starts; restart it after changing them or updating wdx.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`wdx daemon restart`](#wdx-daemon-restart) | Restart the daemon, or start it |
| [`wdx daemon start`](#wdx-daemon-start) | Start the daemon |
| [`wdx daemon status`](#wdx-daemon-status) | Show whether the daemon is running |
| [`wdx daemon stop`](#wdx-daemon-stop) | Stop the daemon |

## wdx daemon restart

Restart the daemon, or start it.

```sh
wdx daemon restart [flags]
```

Stop the daemon if it is running, then start it, as after updating wdx or its settings.

### Examples

```sh
# Restart the daemon after changing the settings
wdx daemon restart
```

### Output

The daemon started. With `--json`: {"result": "restarted", "daemon": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `restarted`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx daemon start

Start the daemon.

```sh
wdx daemon start [--foreground] [flags]
```

Waits until the daemon answers. It starts through systemd or launchd when the installer set it up as a service, else in the background. With `--foreground` it runs in this process until interrupted, as a service manager runs it.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--foreground` |  | run in this process until interrupted |

### Examples

```sh
# Start the daemon
wdx daemon start

# Run it in this terminal until Ctrl-C
wdx daemon start --foreground
```

### Output

The daemon, already running or started; with `--foreground`, the daemon once stopped. With `--json`: {"result": ..., "daemon": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `running`, `started` or `stopped`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`already_running`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#already_running) | 1 | a daemon already serves this home |
| [`daemon_unavailable`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#daemon_unavailable) | 3 | the daemon is not running or not answering |
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx daemon status

Show whether the daemon is running.

```sh
wdx daemon status [flags]
```

Show whether the daemon is running

### Examples

```sh
# Show whether the daemon is running
wdx daemon status

# As JSON
wdx daemon status --json
```

### Output

Whether the daemon is running, its pid, what it says about itself when it answers, and the service manager that runs it, if it is installed as a service. With `--json`: {"running": ..., "pid": ..., "daemon": {...}, "manager": ...}

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |

## wdx daemon stop

Stop the daemon.

```sh
wdx daemon stop [flags]
```

The requests in flight finish first. It stops through systemd or launchd when it runs as a service, else by signalling it.

### Examples

```sh
# Stop the daemon
wdx daemon stop
```

### Output

The daemon stopped, or that none was running. With `--json`: {"result": ..., "daemon": {...}}

With `--json`, `result` is one of: `not_running` or `stopped`.

### Errors

| Code | Exit | When |
|---|---|---|
| [`usage`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#usage) | 2 | the request, command line or a setting is invalid |
| [`internal`](/wdx/docs/reference/errors/#internal) | 3 | an unexpected failure: database, filesystem or git |
